content:
Let \(N\) be a 10-digit number, so
\[
10^9 \le N < 10^{10}.
\]
If \(N^2\) had 20 digits, then the first 10 digits being \(N\) would mean
\[
N \le \frac{N^2}{10^{10}} < N+1.
\]
The left inequality gives \(N\ge 10^{10}\), impossible. Hence \(N^2\) has 19 digits.

Thus the condition is
\[
N \le \frac{N^2}{10^9} < N+1.
\]
The left inequality is automatic for \(N\ge 10^9\). The right inequality gives
\[
N^2 < (N+1)10^9.
\]
Write \(N=10^9+k\) with \(k\ge 0\). Then
\[
(10^9+k)^2 < (10^9+k+1)10^9,
\]
which simplifies to
\[
k^2+(k-1)10^9<0.
\]
For \(k\ge 1\), the left side is nonnegative, so only \(k=0\) works.

Therefore,
\[
N=10^9=1000000000.
\]

\[
\boxed{1000000000}
\]
